title: Water caustics traced onto a pool floor
purpose: Generate tileable maps of caustic light focused by a wavy water surface onto a floor: rays refracted through a periodic surface are splatted onto pool tiles, rippled sand, rock or a grey card, and the emissive map holds the light. Use for pools, shallow seas, aquariums and as a projected light cookie.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python water_caustics.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: wave_cells
parameters.meaning: Main wave features across the tile; more cells give a finer caustic web.

parameters.name: focus
parameters.meaning: Water depth times refraction strength: low gives soft blotches, high sharp folded lines.

parameters.name: ripples
parameters.meaning: Fine ripples on the surface that break the web into smaller cells.

parameters.name: light
parameters.meaning: Brightness of the focused light in the emissive map.

parameters.name: floor
parameters.meaning: Floor under the water: 0 pool tiles, 1 rippled sand, 2 rough rock, 3 plain grey card.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo and the light in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Swimming pool: sharp bright web over pale blue glazed tiles.

presets.name: sandy_shallows
presets.description: Tropical shallows: turquoise light over rippled sand, finer web.

presets.name: deep_reef
presets.description: Deeper water: soft, dim blue caustics over dark rock.

presets.name: light_cookie
presets.description: High-contrast caustic light on a plain grey card, for projecting as light.

limits: One still frame, not an animation. Refraction uses the paraxial approximation (ray offset proportional to the surface slope), light falls straight down and there is no dispersion, absorption or depth-dependent blur, so it is an approximation of real caustics rather than a light transport simulation. Brightness comes from four rays per output pixel and a light smoothing filter, so the finest lines are about a pixel wide at any size. The floor types are simple; the emissive map holds colour only, so the engine sets the emission strength.
technique_references: Paraxial refraction of vertical light through a height field
Photon splatting: ray density by bilinear deposition with wrap-around
Fractional Brownian motion on two incommensurate lattices for the water surface
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
